records.finding: Algorithms 1-2 support neighbor-set skeleton search, stored separators and collider/orientation rules. Theorems 1-2 require independent Gaussian vectors faithful to a sparse DAG, polynomial dimension growth, a nonzero partial-correlation lower bound and vanishing testing level. The manuscript retains these conditions and explicitly separates oracle recovery from finite-sample certification or arbitrary nonlinear time-series discovery.

Definitions 1-3, the inducing-path construction and the oracle discussion support the indexed MAG/PAG and m-separation semantics. A directed MAG edge establishes observed ancestry without excluding every hidden confounding route in the underlying DAG. Circle marks vary across admissible whole-graph completions. The manuscript and commercial comparison correctly distinguish latent mixture classes from causal equivalence classes and retain the source's exclusion of selection, whose inclusion needs broader ancestral graphs and extra rules.

Theorem 1 gives the exact-zero trace-exponential characterization using nonnegative closed-walk terms. Both manuscript contexts reproduce that mathematical property while separating numerical tolerances, optimization stationarity, causal sufficiency and causal identification. No global optimum or causal graph uniqueness is attributed to the acyclicity identity.

Sections 2.2-2.3 require innovations independent across components and time, non-Gaussianity and an acyclic instantaneous coefficient matrix. ICA identifies the mixing with scale/permutation indeterminacy; acyclicity and diagonal normalization resolve the stated correspondence. The manuscript uses precisely these restrictions for structural VAR identification and does not equate forecasting gains with causal identification.

Sections 2.1-2.3 specify a stationary acyclic structural time-series model with independent innovations, latent variables, faithfulness and no selection. Earlier observed history is marginalized outside the chosen lag window, so longer windows can remove old-window adjacencies. The source targets a stationarity-constrained ancestral equivalence object, as the manuscript explains; its oracle statement does not certify finite-data endpoints or arbitrary selected bank samples.

Definition 3.2 and Proposition 3.4 distinguish repeating ancestry/orientations from repeating adjacency at finite boundaries. Sections 4.5-4.6 show why the then-current LPCMCI target can miss invariants of the stronger time-series class and give conceptual enumeration with a practical computational limitation. Propositions 5.2-5.7 show the information gained with larger windows. The manuscript identifies this as the inspected 2021 preprint and keeps independent two-period episode experiments separate from stationary infinite-history guarantees.

Assumptions 1 require causal sufficiency, Markov and adjacency-faithfulness conditions, consistent CI decisions, stationarity, time order and sufficient maximum lag, excluding selection and measurement error. Theorem 2 distinguishes conservative collider orientation from majority/standard rules that need standard faithfulness. Both manuscript contexts preserve these restrictions and allow unresolved contemporaneous directions.

Section 3 uses causal sufficiency and PC assumptions plus missingness indicators that do not cause substantive variables, faithful observability, restrictions among indicators and no self-masking. The manuscript accurately states that its correction is not a general MNAR solution and that test-wise selected samples can create spurious graph relations.

Sections 3.2-3.3 specify additive corruption and masking with approximately low-rank true covariates; ordinary deterministic rounding is explicitly outside the class. Section 4 combines training-only cleaning, error-in-variable regression/balancing and split-sample estimation, with implicit cleaning preserving test independence. The manuscript correctly attributes a structured cleaning/inference procedure rather than a general permission to apply PCA followed by ordinary standard errors or arbitrary informative-missingness correction.

Assumptions A1-A5 require specific conditional mismatch, outcome, treatment and incorrect-pair independence restrictions with overlap. The audit subsection additionally requires membership independent of all variables and truthful match labels. All four indexed contexts preserve these restrictions, distinguish matcher scores from calibrated mismatch probabilities and label unequal-inclusion/persistent-pair corrections as project constructions rather than inherited results.

Sections 2.2-2.3 contrast nested full value solutions with coordinated parameter simulation and kernel-weighted updates from past iterations. Assumptions 1-8 and Theorems 1-2 impose compactness, bounded/Lipschitz components, discounting, growing memory and shrinking-bandwidth conditions. The manuscript accurately withholds this convergence guarantee from arbitrary MCMC with one approximate Bellman update.
